note: Vectors computed directly from the shipped kernel. Covers a clean tie-out with a designed plug fully explaining the gap (RECON_DESIGNED_PLUG_APPLIED), a genuine break routed to review_required, a quarter-end GL-not-yet-closed did_not_run kept distinct from a genuine break, and a cadence-refused did_not_run where a daily request meets a monthly-only underlying schedule.

vectors.name: clean-tie-out-with-designed-plug
vectors.description: FR 2052a-style monthly reconciliation, two accounts. Account GL-1001 carries a non-zero designed plug (S.B.6 Carrying Value Adjustment) that fully explains the gap between the reported and GL figures, so the residual after netting the plug is zero. Account GL-1002 ties out exactly with no plug. RECON_TIE_OUT_CLEAN, RECON_DESIGNED_PLUG_APPLIED.

rationale: Versioned policy inputs: appendix/schedule version FR2052a-AppVIII-2026Q2, source FR 2052a Appendix VIII, rev 2026-Q2 (firm-by-firm alignment).
Reporting cadence monthly against underlying schedule cadence monthly.
2 account(s) evaluated, 0 outside tolerance after the declared plug, 1 carrying a non-zero designed plug.
Every account ties out within its declared tolerance after netting the designed plug.

This is an arithmetic tie-out over the figures supplied for this cycle against a caller-declared general-ledger figure, the only independent witness in this reconciliation program. It does not itself pull the GL balance and is not a determination that any underlying control has been met.
output_payload.note: Deterministic tie-out of a caller-declared reported figure to a caller-declared general-ledger figure, by account, against the general ledger as an independent book of record -- unlike sibling nodes in this programme that compare only declared-vs-declared. A designed plug is a first-class declared input, netted before the residual and never counted as a break. A daily-cadence request against a less-frequent underlying schedule, or a GL not yet declared closed, refuses to run rather than emit a misleading pass or a false break; the two are reported as distinct did_not_run reasons.
